title: Inbound Network Signal Hub and Remediation Catalog for Air‑gapped Private Requests
creator: Alex Chen
description: Create a consolidated intake 'signal hub' and remediation catalog for Private/VPC/on‑prem customer requests that are blocked by network constraints (air‑gapped, proxy-only, strict egress policies, legacy firewall/whitelist requirements). The hub will normalize incoming request signals, score risk/readiness, and map to a prescriptive remediation catalog with customer‑facing steps, automated probes, and recommended engineering playbooks. Goal: reduce TTR for network-blocked requests, provide predictable SLAs and a self‑serve fastpass for low-risk cases.
acceptance_criteria: A triage signal schema defined and documented (network-signal taxonomy) that covers at minimum: egress rules, proxy type, port restrictions, TLS interception, outbound IP constraints, KMS/HSM access requirements, and airgap classification.
An automated self‑service probe (beta) that customers can run to generate a normalized readiness report and prefill the intake form (links + sample output).

A remediation catalog with at least 12 discrete remediation recipes (proxy bridge, managed NAT egress, certificate pinning guidance, DNS whitelisting patterns, staged sync windows, edge connector template) and owner assignments for each recipe.
Triage scoring rubric implemented in the intake UI that surfaces an initial lane: Fastpass (self-serve), Assisted Onboarding, or Concierge (requires on-site/engineering assisted).
SLA definitions for each lane and an internal routing rule set to assign to Partner Engineering, Solutions, or Escalations queues.
Playbooks and at least two sample customer comms templates for Fastpass and Concierge lanes uploaded to Confluence and linked in the intake flow.
Runbook for tracking and measuring time-to-remediation and conversion rates for Fastpass attempts with telemetry surfaced in Console within 1 release.
Security review completed and a checklist for KMS/HSM and compliance constraints embedded in the catalog items.
